title: The Spirit Breathes upon the Word
description: The Spirit Breathes upon the Word in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 62, “The light and glory of the word”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Spir-it breathes up-on the word, And brings the truth to sight; Pre-cepts and prom-is-es af-ford A sanc-ti-fy-ing light.

lines: The Spirit breathes upon the word,
And brings the truth to sight;
A glory gilds the sacred page,
It gives a light to every age,
The hand that gave it, still supplies
His truths upon the nations rise,
As makes a world of darkness shine
The steps of him I love;
Till glory breaks upon my view

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
